cards.name: The Alamo
cards.summary: Use the free reserved church visit or a paid experience for concise city context, not as a universal half-day.

cards.name: GO RIO narrated cruise
cards.summary: A seated 35-minute city orientation; boarding, weather, and the wait still need a current check.

cards.name: The DoSeum
cards.summary: The clearest hands-on younger-child anchor, with indoor exhibits, outdoor play, and an official Calm Corner.

cards.name: Hemisfair and Yanaguana Garden
cards.summary: Use this free play-and-reset stop between Downtown commitments, subject to weather and current park notices.

cards.name: San Antonio Zoo
cards.summary: A substantial animal day with free garage parking; start with a few priorities and treat add-ons separately.

cards.name: Witte Museum
cards.summary: Choose this for Texas nature, science, and culture when the family wants a broader museum than a play space.

cards.name: Japanese Tea Garden
cards.summary: A short, free garden stop that works best as a Brackenridge pairing, not a reason to cross the city alone.

cards.name: San Antonio Missions
cards.summary: Start at Mission San Jose for the visitor center and Junior Ranger context; do not assume all four sites share hours.

cards.name: San Antonio Botanical Garden
cards.summary: A nature-led family block with a Family Adventure Garden; splash use, events, hours, and heat are date-specific.

cards.name: Morgan's Wonderland
cards.cost: Paid; guests with special needs free
cards.summary: An inclusive theme-park choice with 25-plus rides and play elements; calendar and exact attraction needs decide fit.

cards.name: Natural Bridge Caverns
cards.summary: Choose the exact cavern tour first; terrain, duration, above-ground add-ons, and drive time change the family day.

cards.name: Six Flags Fiesta Texas
cards.summary: A ride-led full day when height splits and thrill interests work across the family; check the dated calendar and closures.

cards.name: SeaWorld San Antonio
cards.summary: A full-day mix of animals, presentations, and rides; Aquatica requires a separate ticket choice and schedules vary.

pages.source_note: Official attraction and city sources checked July 23, 2026. Recheck tickets, hours, exhibitions, weather, water conditions, and operating details for the exact visit date.

cards.name: Field Museum
cards.summary: Choose two or three exhibit priorities and treat this as the day's museum, not the first of several.

cards.name: Shedd Aquarium
cards.summary: A strong animal and indoor anchor when the family is comfortable with timed tickets and busy galleries.

cards.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
cards.summary: Hands-on exhibits can fill most of a day; Hyde Park travel and ticketed add-ons make it a deliberate choice.

cards.name: Adler Planetarium
cards.summary: Best when space or sky shows are the real interest, not merely as a third Museum Campus stop.

cards.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
cards.summary: Free admission and flexible exits make this one of the easiest choices to shorten around weather or energy.

cards.name: Millennium Park and Maggie Daley Park
cards.summary: Use the parks as a first-day orientation or movement break, with the Play Garden strongest for children under 12.

cards.name: Chicago Architecture Center river cruise
cards.summary: A signature older-kid choice when the family can sit for 90 minutes and plans around weather and departure time.

cards.name: Chicago Children's Museum
cards.summary: The clearest family reason to visit Navy Pier, with hands-on play aimed mainly at younger children.

cards.name: Art Institute of Chicago
cards.summary: A short family route can work better than a completionist visit; family resources and sensory guidance are available.

cards.name: 360 CHICAGO
cards.summary: A contained skyline choice; treat TILT as an optional add-on and check visibility before committing.

cards.name: Garfield Park Conservatory
cards.summary: A calm greenhouse reset with lower ticket pressure; check the current resident and nonresident admission model.

cards.name: Chicago lakefront and beach time
cards.summary: Keep this flexible and choose the exact beach or path only after checking season, weather, swim status, and facilities.

cards.name: Central Park
cards.summary: Choose one playground, lawn, or museum-adjacent zone; the park is too large to treat as one simple stop.

cards.name: American Museum of Natural History
cards.summary: Pick two or three halls and make this the day's museum rather than the first of several large attractions.

cards.name: Staten Island Ferry
cards.summary: A free harbor crossing with skyline and Statue views; schedule, boarding, waiting, and the return still need a plan.

cards.name: Children's Museum of Manhattan
cards.summary: A purpose-built younger-child choice; strollers are checked rather than used in exhibit areas.

cards.name: Top of the Rock
cards.summary: A contained skyline choice when the family accepts timed entry, weather-dependent views, and a premium ticket.

cards.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park
cards.summary: Choose a pier or playground before arrival and use the waterfront as a flexible skyline and movement block.

cards.name: Intrepid Museum
cards.summary: Aviation, naval, and space exhibits justify a major block; vessel spaces and outdoor decks make access and weather specific.

cards.name: New York Transit Museum
cards.summary: Historic trains are a strong transit-loving choice, but the decommissioned station has stairs and limited climate control.

cards.name: New York Hall of Science
cards.summary: Hands-on science can carry a half-day; the Queens route and any add-ons make it a deliberate anchor.

cards.name: Bronx Zoo
cards.summary: Treat the large zoo as the day's commitment and choose a few priority areas rather than trying to cover every exhibit.

cards.name: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
cards.summary: A historic harbor day with authorized ferry tickets, security, waits, and optional pedestal or crown access to decide in advance.

cards.name: High Line
cards.summary: A free linear city walk with art and street views; confirm the working elevator and choose an exit before starting.
